title: Microsoft Teams: Awards and Certifications badges on profile cards
summary: Hold: the assurances that this change creates no new data store and changes neither sign-in nor permissions are not established by Microsoft's published text. The rollout, automatic display and both Graph delete operations are supported; the licensing description and impact rating also need small corrections.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no feature-specific licence requirement is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' and licensing.notes to 'Each user in the organisation must have a Teams licence before using Teams, except for joining meetings anonymously. Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to Awards and Certifications display.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. The standard treats this product-level entitlement beside an unpublished feature-specific requirement as an understatement, not a blocker.

claims.claim: Impact is low even though the rationale says every Teams user opening a populated card sees the automatic change.
claims.quote: impact: "low"; Where they are populated, every Teams user who opens a card sees it. Standard: Impact low means admins only, or a small opt-in group; high means most users, or a change to default behaviour.
claims.fix: Set impact to 'high' and replace its rationale with 'High. In organisations that populate Awards and Certifications, the section appears automatically for all users; organisations with empty properties see no visible change.' The tenant-data prerequisite does not make the viewers an opt-in group.
